title: Splitting state, and importing infrastructure that already exists

videos.script: Ana's shop had one state, and everything lived in it. The network, the security group, every bucket. {{one}} Tagging one bucket meant asking AWS about all six resources. And one careless edit to the app could reach the VPC. {{split}} So she cut the state in two. The network changes a few times a year. The app changes every week. Each gets its own key in the bucket. {{keys}} The app still needs the network's VPC. It reads it from the network's outputs, which are a promise, not a guess. {{outputs}} Then the data team took over a bucket. Ana's state let go of it, and theirs imported it. The bucket itself never moved. {{move}} Last come the resources nobody wrote down. A bucket a colleague made by hand. A security group with a rule in nobody's file. {{import}} Terraform can adopt them, and even write a first draft of their configuration. {{generate}} The rule for all of it is the same. Change the files, and trust nothing until a plan says the real world will not move.
